historicalReview.oldPath: ViewCache.query called /events. Native pack retrieval was conditional on returned native record references and missing local coverage. An empty server result avoided native finalization.
historicalReview.oldPublication: The archived backend already rewrote every source supplied to put; it was not an equality-aware writer. Its transaction already batched file flushes and metadata publication.
historicalReview.regression: 1d972f3 introduced the ordinary now() live-window retrieval path. Its first response can carry sealed branch manifests already represented locally. NativeStore.finish marks every received manifest source changed; putting unchanged sources then rewrites their layouts and time tries. The check for incoming events is required; these unchanged publications are not.
historicalReview.scope: Keep local matching, whole-hour batching, now() freshness and data-before-trie publication. Do not revert to historical server matching or redesign replication.

setup: Same broad existing replica of 25 demo branches. First search after app reopen, not empty OPFS. Query: events | where duration >= 10000; Today UTC ending at now(). Public HTTPS origin snoot.trietrunk.com. No storage reset. Baseline and deployed measurements use clean, uninstrumented app bundles.
methodology: Three searches per app session. Each result must be complete, have increased usage and lastUsedAt at or after the click, avoiding a previously persisted measurement. elapsedMs is application data-ready timing and excludes painting. observedAfterClickMs includes automation and 100ms completion polling; it is not a paint measurement. Small sequential sample, no percentile claim.

diagnostics.note: Per-file diagnostic instrumentation used a separate unlinked build. The earlier reproduction precedes the shared-cache-budget fix; compare operation counts, not its elapsed time directly with the clean baseline above.

changes: Skip metadata publication when all supplied sources and control equal the committed immutable snapshots.
Keep just-published decoded snapshots in the existing bounded cache.
Read retirement headers and write only actual changes, avoiding unnecessary dirty-file flushes.
